title: Laplace coefficient formula for a selected column set
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\ge0$, and $Q$ a $q\times q$ matrix over $R$ [def-weil-matrix]. Write $[q]=\{1,\ldots,q\}$. For subsets $I,T\subseteq[q]$ of the same cardinality, $Q_{I,T}$ denotes the square submatrix with its rows and columns in increasing order [def-weil-submatrix], and $\det$ denotes [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]. For every $0\le s\le q$ and every $s$-element column set $T\subseteq[q]$, one has the coefficient identity
$$\det Q=\sum_{\substack{I\subseteq[q]\\|I|=s}}(-1)^{\sum_{i\in I}i+\sum_{j\in T}j}\det(Q_{I,T})\det(Q_{[q]\setminus I,[q]\setminus T}).$$
All signs are mapped from $\mathbf Z$ to $R$. Complements and all submatrices retain increasing order; no permutation sign is suppressed. This includes $s=0$, $s=q$, and $q=0$, with empty determinant and empty product equal to $1$. Thus this is an identity giving specified complementary-minor coefficients, for an arbitrary retained column set, rather than an assertion of membership in an ideal.

proof.text: Expand $\det Q$ as $\sum_{\sigma\in S_q}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_{j=1}^qQ_{\sigma(j),j}$ using [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]. Fix $T=(t_1<\cdots<t_s)$ and list its complement as $(u_1<\cdots<u_{q-s})$. Reindex the finite sum by $I=\sigma(T)$ and two permutations $\alpha\in S_s$, $\beta\in S_{q-s}$. Indeed, if $I=(i_1<\cdots<i_s)$ and $I^c=(v_1<\cdots<v_{q-s})$, the inverse sends $(I,\alpha,\beta)$ to the map $t_a\mapsto i_{\alpha(a)}$, $u_b\mapsto v_{\beta(b)}$. Its two restrictions are bijective onto disjoint complementary sets, so it is a permutation. Each restriction recovers its unique $\alpha$ or $\beta$; thus the constructions are inverse and every term occurs exactly once.

source.place: Tag 07Z7, lemma-ideals-generated-by-minors, expansion hint; explicit agent-supplied Leibniz grouping, step 1

proof.text: For the permutation indexed by $(I,\alpha,\beta)$, apply [lem-trf-ordered-block-permutation-sign] with the increasing lists just chosen. Its hypothesis $\sigma(T)=I$ holds by construction, and it gives $\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)=\epsilon(I,T)\operatorname{sgn}(\alpha)\operatorname{sgn}(\beta)$, where $\epsilon(I,T)=(-1)^{\sum I+\sum T}$. Apply the canonical ring map $\mathbf Z\to R$ to this integer equality.

source.place: Tag 07Z7, lemma-ideals-generated-by-minors, expansion hint; explicit agent-supplied Leibniz grouping, step 2

proof.text:
Split each product over the disjoint sets $T$ and $T^c$. The contribution for fixed $I$ is therefore
$$\epsilon(I,T)\left(\sum_{\alpha\in S_s}\operatorname{sgn}(\alpha)\prod_{a=1}^s Q_{i_{\alpha(a)},t_a}\right)\left(\sum_{\beta\in S_{q-s}}\operatorname{sgn}(\beta)\prod_{b=1}^{q-s}Q_{v_{\beta(b)},u_b}\right).$$
This is finite distributivity: multiplying the two sums chooses each pair $(\alpha,\beta)$ once, and commutativity of $R$ permits the displayed grouping. By [def-weil-submatrix] and [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant], the two parentheses are precisely $\det(Q_{I,T})$ and $\det(Q_{I^c,T^c})$, with increasing orders. Summing these contributions over $I$ gives the claimed formula.

source.place: Tag 07Z7, lemma-ideals-generated-by-minors, expansion hint; explicit agent-supplied Leibniz grouping, step 3

proof.text: For $s=0$ the only row set is empty; its sign exponent is $0$, and its determinant is $1$ by [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant], so the term is $\det Q$. For $s=q$ the only row set is $[q]$; the exponent is $2\sum_{i=1}^qi$ and hence even, while the complementary determinant is $1$. If $q=0$, necessarily $s=0$, all the sums over permutations have one term, all products are empty, and both sides are $1$. These calculations require no cancellation or invertibility in $R$.
